events.title: Cortés Enters Tenochtitlan
events.description: Spanish conquistador Hernán Cortés entered the Aztec capital of Tenochtitlan. Emperor Moctezuma II welcomed him with great ceremony.
events.significance: The meeting began a chain of events that led to the fall of the Aztec Empire and the establishment of Spanish colonial rule in Mexico.

events.title: Battle of White Mountain
events.description: Near Prague, an army of about 15,000 Bohemians and mercenaries was routed by a larger force of Imperial and Catholic League troops. The battle took place early in the Thirty Years' War.
events.significance: The defeat ended the Bohemian revolt and strengthened Habsburg control over Bohemia. It was an early turning point in one of Europe's most destructive wars.

events.title: Montana Becomes the 41st State
events.description: Montana was admitted to the Union as the 41st U.S. state. It joined the Union in the same period as several other northwestern territories.
events.significance: Statehood marked the maturing of the American West. The new state's copper and other mining wealth was important to the national economy.

events.title: Röntgen Discovers X-rays
events.description: While experimenting with electricity in his laboratory, German physicist Wilhelm Röntgen noticed a new kind of penetrating radiation. He called it X-rays.
events.significance: The discovery transformed medicine by letting doctors see inside the body without surgery. It earned Röntgen the first Nobel Prize in Physics in 1901.

events.title: Birth of Margaret Mitchell
events.description: American novelist Margaret Mitchell was born in Atlanta, Georgia. She later wrote the best-selling novel Gone with the Wind.
events.significance: Her only published novel won the Pulitzer Prize and became one of the best-selling books of all time. It also inspired a landmark film adaptation.
